n.dropwrong1: And what exactly is that supposed to do?
n.typo_done: Yes, yes, you already found that one. Stop rubbing it in.
h.none: No ideas right now. Odd: I usually have too many.
card.ch8.label: Chapter 8
card.ch8.title: The Glossary
end.ch8.title: End of Chapter 8
end.ch8.body:
The guard dog is a cake, the siren sings and the gate is a fan. The glossary will never be the same.
In Chapter 9 the box gets turned over.
page.p26.title: Glossary (C–G)
page.p26.intro: Everything in GRAND ADVENTURE DELUXE is exactly what the glossary says.
page.p26.margin: the definitions are stuck on like the words
page.p27.title: Glossary (S–W)
n.i1: The Print Shop Guardhouse. Beyond that gate the Proofreader is preparing the final edition.
n.i2: There's a guard dog. There's an alarm siren. There's a gate. The Proofreader has thought of everything.
p.i1: he's thought of everything that's written down. look at the glossary.
n.i3: The glossary explains words, it doesn't change them. That's its only rule.
n.i4: Page 26. Everything is exactly what the glossary says. So don't touch it.
n.empty1: Bricks, bricks, bricks. Very reassuring, for a guardhouse.
n.empty2: Nothing there. The definitions are in the manual.
n.tool1: The arrows won't help here. The right words will.
n.typo_dog: "Doog". A dog with two Os. Twice the bark.
n.siren: The alarm siren. If the gate opens without permission, it wails. Loudly.
n.mermaid_sing: The siren is singing. Badly, but with feeling. No alarm in sight.
n.whale: A poster of a singing whale. The Guardhouse likes music.
n.whale_alarm: The whale is now an alarm that wails. It has a beacon on its head. Don't ask me how.
n.cake: A birthday cake. Whose birthday? The dog's, I bet.
n.cake_barks: The cake is barking. It's an animal that barks, says the glossary. Don't eat it.
n.dog1: WOOF! The guard dog won't let you near.
n.dog2: The Proofreader's dog. It bites misplaced commas.
n.dog_cake_tap: It's a cake. It's still wearing its collar. And it's a bit offended.
n.gate_closed: The gate: a barrier that never opens. The glossary says so.
n.gate_dog: The gate is open, but the guard dog won't let you through. WOOF.
n.cake1: The dog... has turned into a cake. With a collar.
n.cake2: "DOG: birthday treat". And the cake on the table is barking now. The glossary has gone mad.
n.mermaid1: The alarm siren has become a siren. From the sea. In a fishbowl. Singing.
n.mermaid2: And the whale on the poster is now an alarm. Some definitions should never be swapped.
n.fan1: The gate folded up like a fan. No alarm: the siren is too busy singing.
n.alarm1: The gate opens and the siren WAILS!
n.alarm2: It snapped shut. A barrier that never opens, again. The siren needs silencing first.
n.dog_alarm: "DOG: alarm that wails". So basically nothing has changed.
n.gate_cake: A cake gate. The Proofreader would never forgive it.
n.dog_sing: The dog is a sea creature that sings. It howls, mostly.
n.x1: The gate is open, the dog is a cake, the siren sings. The Proofreader didn't plan for the glossary.
n.x2: Beyond the gate... there's no print shop. There's the back of the box.
p.x1: the print shop is on the other side. first we have to turn the box over.
n.x3: Turn the box over? The game is a box? We're in a box?
p.x2: a box with a manual inside. and an age rating on the back.
h.dog.1: The guard dog blocks the way. On page 26 the glossary says what a dog is.
h.dog.2: Definitions come loose like words. What would you like that dog to be?
h.siren.1: If the gate opens, the siren wails. The siren must be silenced first.
h.siren.2: SIREN has two meanings. On page 27 a whale sings beautifully.
h.siren.3: Swap "sea creature that sings" (WHALE) with "alarm that wails" (SIREN).
h.gate.1: The gate is "a barrier that never opens". You need something that opens.
h.gate.2: On page 27 there's a thing that opens and closes.
h.gate.3: Swap the definition of FAN with that of GATE (after silencing the siren), then tap the gate.
